settings.taxPostingSubtitle: Where recoverable purchase tax posts in NetSuite.
settings.taxPostingHelp: Recoverable GST/HST and QST post to these accounts as their own lines, on both card transactions and expense reports. Tax that cannot be reclaimed is capitalised into the expense line instead and needs no account.
settings.postingTriggerSubtitle: Who decides that an approved report reaches the general ledger.

postingTriggerHelp.AP_QUEUE: An approved report waits in Posting until somebody reads its payload and sends it. Nothing reaches NetSuite unreviewed, and the half-hourly catch-up sweep sends nothing either.
postingTriggerHelp.AUTOMATIC: The final approval posts the report straight away, and a half-hourly sweep re-sends anything that was missed or failed on a transient error. Posting then lists only what failed or was withheld. Switching to this sends every approved report already waiting, on the next passes.

settings.taxGroupsSubtitle: The tax group every posted expense line carries, for each nexus NetSuite reports under.
settings.taxGroupsNoneSynced: No tax groups have been synced yet. Run a reference sync, then choose one for each nexus.
settings.taxGroupsNoLegalEntity: No legal entity is in a country NetSuite reports a nexus for.
settings.taxGroupsPostingRule: Posting uses the group for the submitter's legal entity country
settings.taxGroupOnlyClearable: No other {country} group is synced; this default can only be cleared
settings.taxGroupsHelp: Choose a zero-rated group. ExpenseOS already works out the tax — recoverable GST/QST post as their own GL lines and the rest is included in the line it belongs to — so a group with a rate would have NetSuite charge tax on tax. Without a tax code, NetSuite refuses a Canadian report outright.

people.intro: Where ExpenseOS and NetSuite disagree about a person. The sync never picks a side; you do.
people.empty: Nothing to review — every field NetSuite holds agrees with ExpenseOS.
people.divergesHelp: Adopted from NetSuite while Google still says otherwise. Google is never overwritten by ExpenseOS — ask HR or IT to correct the upstream record; this clears itself when Google agrees.
people.unmappedHelp: NetSuite holds this value, and no ExpenseOS record is mapped to it — so ExpenseOS cannot adopt it. Keeping ExpenseOS still works and is usually what you want here: it pushes the ExpenseOS value to NetSuite and corrects the NetSuite record. To adopt it instead, map the NetSuite record to an ExpenseOS one first.
people.noteHelp: Optional. The decision is the record; the note is why.
people.ruleText: ADP is the source of truth for who a person is. Google follows ADP, ExpenseOS follows Google, and NetSuite is consulted last. Keeping ExpenseOS pushes the value to NetSuite. Adopting NetSuite writes its value onto the person and pins it, then flags HR / IT until Google agrees — ExpenseOS never overwrites Google.
people.rulingKeepHelp: NetSuite’s employee record is updated with this value. One attempt; a failure shows on the row and can be retried.
people.rulingAdoptHelp: The person is updated with NetSuite’s value and the field is pinned so the nightly Google sync does not put the old value back. The row stays open, marked HR / IT, until Google agrees.
people.rulingAdoptClassHelp: The person is updated with NetSuite’s class. Google holds no class, so this resolves the row immediately.
people.dismissTitle: Dismiss {count, plural, one {# discrepancy} other {# discrepancies}}
people.dismissHelp: For a difference that is nobody’s mistake. It stays dismissed while these two values stand; a change on either side reopens it.
people.pushErrorHelp: NetSuite’s own words, exactly as it returned them. A short or cryptic message is a NetSuite-side error, not an ExpenseOS one.
people.pushAdminRecord: NetSuite refuses edits to an administrator’s employee record.
people.pushAdminRecordHelp: This is a NetSuite security rule, not a problem with the integration: only an administrator may edit an administrator’s record. Change this field in NetSuite directly — retrying is harmless, but it will be refused the same way.
people.pushQueued: Queued — NetSuite will be updated by the worker in a moment.
people.adoptedPinned: Adopted NetSuite’s value and pinned it. The row stays open for HR / IT until Google agrees.

run.title: Run the employee sync now
run.intro: Pull every employee from NetSuite and reconcile them with the people in ExpenseOS. It normally runs once a night, behind the directory sync.
run.liveHelp: A live run fills in the business unit, department, legal entity, class and manager that are still blank on real people, using what NetSuite holds, and opens a review row here wherever the two systems hold different values. It never overwrites a value ExpenseOS already has.
run.dryHelp: A dry run reads NetSuite and reports exactly what a live run would do. It writes nothing.
run.pending: Running against NetSuite. This can take a minute or two — leave this open.
run.failed: The employee sync did not run.
run.resultDry: Dry run — nothing was written. This is what a live run would do:
